## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by large, flattened cells divided into two symmetrical semicells by a deep central constriction. Euastrum ventricosum has broadly rounded to somewhat rectangular semicells with several lateral swellings or lobes and resembles Euastrum crassum, although it is generally more elongated in outline. It occurs primarily in cool, acidic to moderately nutrient-poor freshwater habitats such as bog pools, peatlands, and shallow ponds. The species appears to be relatively uncommon and is especially associated with oligotrophic to mesotrophic wetland environments. Like other desmids, it contributes to freshwater primary production and can serve as an indicator of water chemistry and habitat quality.
